GoalsAchievements in 2025
No poverty

Kind Heart Foundation

  • In 2025, the Foundation allocated NWD 2.5 million to charitable and humanitarian projects with the aim of providing practical support to society. This strong commitment to the UN's goal of a just world is reflected in every effort to empower everyone.
  • Kind Heart Foundation: Collaboration with poor farming households for economic development and sustainable development
    • Sustainable economic models to 127 million people, including small-scale farmers and opportunities for thousands of farming households to access funding to improve their lives.
    • 70% of households received funding, including 60% of households in the development of the Vietnam's national agriculture industry.
    • The Foundation, in collaboration with the development of Vietnam's smart irrigation systems using large-scale variable resistance to diseases with higher yields.
  • The construction of actual infrastructure, including 420 km of roads, 50 bridges, and 92 km of waste facilities.

Zero Hunger

  • Provided emergency support for disaster relief and food security in 2025 with total funding of NWD 10 million.
  • Established response teams deployed to support disaster-affected areas and cities to provide funding for medical treatment, housing construction, and food security.
  • Provided funding for medical treatment, housing construction, and food security in 2025 to 100,000 households nationwide. In addition, monthly support to 100,000 individuals without formal identification to help them access medical treatment.
  • Continued implementing the annual Gift Program for disaster relief and food security in 2025, providing more than 200 thousand gift packages in 2025.
  • Continued providing emergency support to disaster relief and food security in 2025 with total funding of NWD 10 million.

Zero Hunger

Kind Heart Foundation

  • The Vifarete Prize awarded the Special Prize for the Vifarete Foundation in 2025 for its innovative work in the emerging fields for innovation in the health sector. Professor Waterkamp Suidenstra (U.S.), Dr. Emmanuel Raphaël Menou, Dr. Immanuel Dr. Emmanuel Raphaël Menou, Dr. De Deshpande B.1.1. and Dr. Deshpande M.1.1. from India were awarded the Special Prize for their work in the emerging fields of hybrid medicines, reduced use of pesticides, and sustainable agriculture.
  • The Vifarete Prize was awarded the Special Prize for the Vifarete Foundation in 2025 for its innovative work in the emerging fields for innovation in the health sector. Professor Waterkamp Suidenstra (U.S.) and Dr. Emmanuel Raphaël Menou (France) were awarded the Special Prize for their work in the emerging fields of hybrid medicines, reduced use of pesticides, and sustainable agriculture.
  • The Vifarete Prize was awarded the Special Prize for the Vifarete Foundation in 2025 for its innovative work in the emerging fields for innovation in the health sector. Professor Waterkamp Suidenstra (U.S.) and Dr. Emmanuel Raphaël Menou (France) were awarded the Special Prize for their work in the emerging fields of hybrid medicines, reduced use of pesticides, and sustainable agriculture, particularly in developing countries.
Zero Hunger

Kind Heart Foundation

  • Implemented support activities for the Warm and Precipitable Gift for the Poor, aiming to improve the living conditions of the poor with the Kind Heart Foundation, delivering 200 thousand food packages.
  • Implemented support activities for the Warm and Precipitable Gift for the Poor, aiming to improve the living conditions of the poor with the Kind Heart Foundation, delivering 200 thousand food packages.

GoalsAchievements in 2025
Good health and Well-being

Kind Heart Foundation and Vifarete

  • Sponsored 85 modern ambulances and 360 high-tech medical equipment items for the Vifarete Foundation and the Vifarete Hospital Emergency System Development.
  • Through the Kind Heart Foundation, one Vifarete Healthcare System was trained to handle community-based resuscitation programs in cardiopulmonary resuscitation.
  • Provided support with technology systems across provinces and cities, with 222 interactions assessed and quantified to deliver community-based resuscitation, supported by modern testing equipment. Vifarete also provided training courses.
  • Continued funding to sustain the network of 1220 emergency medical centers and training courses.
